From: L.G. Baumann, SOUTH AFRICA






Dear Brian,

I have sent you this letter by
email although I know you pref-
er discs.It is not too long but
I did not want to risk delays as
happened when I previously wrote
and everything was lost in the
mail. Perhaps you could mention
in Outlet whether this is acc-
eptable and whether you have a
means for automatic conversion
to disc at your end. I have used
32 chars per line.


Thank for your reply in Outlet
for June about my LPRINT problem
using the Lunter emulator for
the Plus D. I faxed Brian Gaff
and he responded promptly by
sending me the latest version
3.05. The printing works well on
all my programs except Tasword
II. I have found a solution to
this which I would like to pass
on to other readers who might
have the same problem with Tas-
word II...


My Tasword already had the
following lines in it for the
Plus D:

278 POKE @ 6,1
286 POKE @ 6,0


However, when Line 280...

RANDOMIZE USR 60038
                  ...is reached,
the computer crashes on the
emulator. This can be avoided by
inserting... Line 279 STOP and
when the program stops, restart
it with CONTinue.

Just what this STOP does or why
it works I have no idea. On my
copy I have entered...

279 PRINT"Enter Cont to LPRINT"
: STOP.

                Regards,

              L.G.Baumann

Brian Cavers to L.G. Baumann

We're perfectly happy to receive
email which we can reasonably
convert to a normal text file.

I got the same result in Tasword
2 but I don't understand it. The
problem seems to be caused by
RANDOMIZE USR (FN p(62472) at
the end of Line 250.This appears
to sort out the print channel.
However, it works without it so
delete it or put a REM just
before it (just after the colon
in the middle of line 250) and
resave Tasword. It then works OK
without stopping.

                      Brian

From Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER

Dear Brian.

A few thoughts on recent points
in Outletters...

It has been mentioned a few
times that DD disks and drives
could become difficult to get as
they are now all HD.

The fact that DD disks and
drives are now becoming less
available in favour of HD should
not for some time cause problems
for DD users. Virtually all 3.5"
HD drives to the SA400 standard
can be used with the Disciple,
+D and +3 because they are in
fact, a dual HD/DD drive.


So when you put in a DD disk
that does not have the extra
hole, the drive automatically
works in the DD mode. Even with
the later higher capacity drives
there are so many 3.5" HD users
that it is going to be some time
before they become obsolete.

Now for the controversial point.
Without going into a long
detailed explanation of the
technicalities to confirm my
findings I will simply say that
for some years I have used 3.5"
HD disks in DD drives without
any problems. Disks with data
saved years ago are still
reliably read so the data is not
being corrupted or lost over
time by the apparent "incorrect
use".

The only thing is that as some
of my drives are now DD/HD (the
later SAM drives were also this
type) that it is necessary to
cover the "HD hole" so the drive
stays in DD mode when this type
of disk is used. Just stick a
small piece on both sides cut
from a sticky label is all that
is needed.

I first tried this when I bought
some HD types "by accident" when
it turned out a box marked DD
had HD inside! Later I bought HD
deliberately because I wanted a
specific colour I could only
find in HD. And I also bought HD
recently as at the time I wanted
a few disks there were only HD
types on offer.


Peter Johnson mentioned a list
of printer codes. There was a
list of printer codes in a past
Outlet(early last year I recall)
that covered both the Epson and
IBM with their variations[OUTLET
111].

With respect of Ink Jet printers
it is worth mentioning that some
at least have a "built in" emul-
ation of either or both the Eps-
on LX/IBM Proprinter so would be
virtually a direct replacement
for a dot matrix with little or
no mods needed to the driving
computer, +D or software.

Unfortunately most adverts sim-
ply relate the printer in terms
of a PC and its various options,


drivers, and software packages
and often the driver and fonts
come on a disk/CD ROM to be
loaded to PC hard drive. You
need to obtain the full techni-
cal specification to find out if
the printer is compatible with
other than a PC and its capabil-
ities as a stand alone with self
contained fonts and does it work
with standard ASCII and ESC
codes.

They are sometimes stated as
"IBM compatible" having a
parallel connector - others use
"Apple Talk" being serial. Some
makes can have either or both
options. In emulation mode these
no doubt relate to the Centron-
ics parallel and RS232 serial.


In conclusion I would have
thought makers would want to
sell their products so make them
compatible with and to replace
the "older" dot matrix printers
on as many different systems as
possible even if "emulation
mode" comes as an optional extra
rather than limit their use.

                 Malcolm Perry

Ron Cavers to Malcolm Perry





Interesting point regarding Ink-
Jet printers. Brian and I had
vaguely discussed possiby
getting one as some of our forms
and letters began to look a bit
"old hat" alongside some of the
stuff coming in from readers.
One of the problems in running a
show like OUTLET is that you
have got to try and keep abreast
of the newer technologies other-
wise you begin to flounder when
readers' queries come in that
relate to stuff we've barely
even heard of much less used.


As always, we have to try and
strike a balance between what
cash is in the pot and what is
really needed - as opposed to
what we would like to buy.

Anyhow, We were just about to
commit to a HP Laser - from a
second-user job lot - when my
Star LC20 packed in and it
became imperative to take action
before the July issue came out.
I had asked about and been
assured that the HP had Epson
emulation when it suddenly occ-
urred to me that they were not
talking about on-board emulation
but about drivers -programs that
sit in memory and convert/inter-
pret codes as required. These
are PC orientated - and, as most


of our printer routines run from
the Spectrum, this was no good
to us.

I therefore plumped for an Epson
Stylus Colour 200. This was the
cheapest in the range (the black
was a little cheaper but not
enough to justify the saving).
The main advantage was that the
standard Epson codes were built-
in and so no re-programming
would be necessary - right?
Wrong!  It was fairly easy to
set up - the colour cartridges
and black ink cartridges sit in
their own plastic units and they
are easily inserted into the
carriage frame holder as requir-
ed. A few test-prints and a
dozen "quick brown foxes" and I
was ready for a "live" trial.

It was then, when I was about to
insert a Chezron letter-headed
paper into the printer, that it
suddenly sank in that the Ink
Jet did not have a manual paper
feed knob so it was impossible
to set the paper to the position
required.

On the Star dot matrix printer I
would wind the paper past the
letter heading, before starting
the print routine in Tasword, to
a known starting point (the base
of the letter head would line-up
with the edge of the top cover)
- but the Stylus would always
start printing at the top of the
page after loading the paper
automatically from the tray at
the back.


Now that was an easy one to get
by - I just inserted nine blank
spaces at the start of any
Tasword document and it fed the
paper past the Chezron header.

However,when running our monthly
database program to produce lab-
els and subscription reminders,
it became obvious that every
print routine would have to have
a patch inserted and - as I
hoped to eventually have the
Star printer repaired - it would
have to include an option to
switch between the Ink-Jet and
the Dot Matrix.

Even a simple option like stick-
ing in the odd envelope to print
an address on it became a chall-
enge...

On the Star,because I knew where
the label position was when
printing, I could just insert an
envelope at that point on the
platen roller and wind it into
place with manual knob - didn't
need to think about it, it was
just automatic.But on the Inkjet
everything has to be inserted up
to a fixed plate on the right-
hand edge and a sliding plate
moved up to the left edge to
keep the paper from twisting
when feeding through.


The other main problem is that
we have huge stocks of disk and
address labels which are on
tractor feed backing and are not
suitable to use with an InkJet.


We managed to get by last month
using an old "banger" dot matrix
held together with sticks and
chewing gum but it caused some
headaches and and the whole
episode contributed towards the
delay in getting out last months
OUTLET magazine.

On the plus side is the great
graphics capability (which we
have not yet fully explored),
the marvellous print quality,
and I can now print my letters
at five in the morning (I'm a
bit of an insomniac) without
waking the rest of the house.

                        Ron

From: J. Woodhead, WEST YORKS.







Dear Sir,

As you can now supply 3.5" discs
in +3 format)for a +3 'B' drive)
I would prefer them in this for-
mat IF IT WILL NOT CAUSE YOU EX-
TRA WORK. Otherwise, +D/Disciple
format please. I have Dominic
Morris's Discdos program now and
so I should be able to read +D
format. I just wonder if there
might be difficulty over, for
instance,the print routines,etc.


Incidentally, I had some diffic-
ulty with the printing routine
in Issue 76 which I bought from
you.  I could not get the RS232
option to work.  I finished up
dismantling the printer (Epson
LQ400) and removing the serial
interface so that it reverted to
the Centronics option. I have no
problem with your current discs.
You seem to have altered your
print out program. What am I do-
ing wrong?

I am very impressed with your
TABLOID layout.

       Yours faithfully,

          J. Woodhead

Brian Cavers to J. Woodhead




There seems to be a bug in Issue
76. In BASIC line 1810, CODE "P"
should be CODE "Z". If that does
not work then the easiest way
out might be to load the text
file into a new issue. If the
filename is the same you need
only switch the disk, eg, the
OUTLETTERS filename, LETTERS1.#
has remained the same from the
first +3 issue (23). If you load
say, OUTLET 120,the current one,
then push in the disk for OUTLET
76 and select B for letters, it
should load the old letters and
you can print it.


Where the file name is different
you need to first find the old
name by doing a CAT of the old
issue and using your judgement
as to the file you want (the
OUTLET text files always end in
.#). Then...

1. Enter +3 BASIC.
2. Enter MERGE "CONTENTS"
3. Enter LIST 30
4. Change the first item from
   "EDIT'L  .#" to the old file
   name you saw in the CAT and
   press ENTER to re-enter the
   line.
5. Enter RUN
6. Put the old issue in Drive A.
7. Select EDITORIAL and the old
   file should load and you can
   then print it.


Note that the old file need not
actually be an editorial, it can
be a DRIVECHAT or INFO or any,
but it is just easier to put it
in as the first item.

This method should work on any
system except that early issues
of OUTLET did not use the .#
terminator so line 200 would
need to be altered too.

                      Brian

     Ilford, Essex, IG6 2NW

1) No, we do not know of any
emulator for the PC which will
read Opus discs.

2) Hmm!?... Again the answer

A possible source of assistance

One member of this club is Johan

Opus format, so probably has the
knowledge, or possibly a program
to do what you require.

Johan Koning's address in 1994

            Mieden 6

From: C Bibby, MANCHESTER

Hello to all at Outlet! And what
a great pleasure it is to be a
frequent reader of your articl-
es. My personal interests here
seem to have an all too common
craving judging from your lett-
ers - a need to know more. Does
it ever end Ron ? Don't think
you'll have an answer for that
one friend. Never mind!

What a fab crop of ZX supporters
all round - WELL DONE OUTLET!
Thanks for keeping these old
flames burning.This is the first
time my words to you have been
attempted via a Tas2 version Ron
- and in the required 32 column
width too. BUSY LAD!


Tas2 now on a 3.5" disc here for
the +3 (ZX syntax which you now
have a set-up for) will also do
the stuff to my printer via both
the +2A & +3 thanks to help of/
from one Lloyd Garland and one
or two others. It has a pain-
fully slow cursor however which
I would like to speed up if any-
one knows how.


For those interested, this vers-
ion of Tas2 takes a mere two
minutes to load from tape. (It's
instantaneous from the ram disc
of the +2A) and instantly Cent-
ronics-compatible without that
need for poking around to get it
to work as long as your printer
is set accurately to ON-LINE.


It gets complicated I know when
all you really want to do is get
going without the need to fiddle
or mess around. To be up and
running from switch-on, two mins
isn't such a bad load period I
think as far as tape loaders go.


Since I now have an assortment
of versions of Tasword all mixed
up in boxes and cupboards, this
one I re-named TAS2A. As stated,
it's +2A compatible hence TAS2A.


I remember some time ago reading
somewhere within the Tas2 BASIC
the word FONT. Mmm, I have to
wonder if Tas2 can be fonted up?
If so HOW?


Well Ron, it wasn't very nice to
hear that you also had suffered
problems from Bull Electrical.
This firm was called J & N Bull
untill around 8/10 year's ago.
About ten years ago my letter to
the editor of the then EE mag
brought me a rapid response and
the inevitable apologies and ex-
cuses plus a long awaited cheque
/refund.

Another firm (or possibly a lone
ranger sort) again a few hundred
miles away from myself also
tried to stab me in the back.
Being bossibly a slightly over-
optimistic type at times I rate
every problem as solvable in
some way if we can only work out
how...


My letter to his local constab-
ulary brought a response. Not
actually expecting anything back
this time it wasn't long before
a cheque arrived here again. My
letter to the TWIT's local bobby
did include word's such as how I
enjoyed helping others in need
now and again.The word'menacing'
was also thrown in for good mea-
sure. I don't know how it all
got solved but it did. The guy
might have been a problem in his
local area already - SCUM.

Without knowing what your own
problem is with BULL, well, one
of your readers might have yet
another answer or two worthy of
browsing over. It would be nice
to read the antics of others.
Mmm. Fab stuff. Cheers. - Colin.

Brian Cavers to Colin Bibby

There is an error in the BASIC
in the Tas2A program you sent.To
load a font you first must enter
BASIC and retype line 4010 to...

LOAD n$ CODE 61184,768; GOTO 20

Enter RUN to restart Tasword and
then you need OUTLET 61. Put it
in the drive with Side B upper-
most and from the TAS2 main menu
select C to customise then F to
load a font. Enter... MINICHAR.2
or MINICHAR.3 or MINICHAR.4 and
a new font should load. Press R,
ENTER, R, ENTER and type a few
words to see the new font. Press
O, ENTER at the main menu then
T, ENTER to resave a new copy of
Tasword to make permanent. Brian

From: S. Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS




Could you please advise in what
issue(s) of OUTLET you published
your investigations/findings
relating to the VideoPlus codes,
and have you made any further
discoveries? Thank you.


                   Malcolm


Ron Cavers to Malcolm Goodman






     I thought I would find this
straight-away using one of the
various indexes that we keep but
was flummoxed until I remembered
Francis Miles detailed index
which also covered letters. And
that's where it proved to be -
Page 28 of Outletters in Issue
No.71- July '93 (I can't believe
that it is over 4 years ago that
I started trying to puzzle out
what system could be used to de-
vise those codes).



I haven't done any further work
on the subject but we did publ-
ish a program in the PC version
of OUTLET (No.17,Aug 94) that
would convert date, time,
channel etc into a valid Video+
number. I had doubts about its
usefulness as it originated in
the Good Ol' USA but we found
that it would generate valid
codes for this country also -and
I have just re-checked and it
came up the correct number for
one of tonight's shows on ITV.
The main quibble is that it
doesn't give enough info to be
able to work out how it does the
calculations. I'll include a
copy of the document that came
with it in case you can ferret
out a titbit of useful info.


I'm also including a disk with
my original text file on it plus
anything else that looks as
though it relates to it - don't
worry about returning the disk,
just recycle it.

Let us know how you get on.

                            Ron

From:Alan Rutherford,NEW ZEALAND

Dear Ron and Brian,

Hello again. I have been wait-
ing for the new version of
PROCROSS to come out. This was
mentioned , I think, in the
January edition of Outlet. But
there is no excuse for not
writing, except that I do not
seem to have much time lately.

I have been drafted onto the
committee of my Bowls Club, and
this is taking up a lot of my
time.I'm on the general committ-
ee and in charge of selection
for the mid-week bowls. This
involves quite a lot of meetings
and letters throughout Christ-
church and other towns.

Also I have been on a bowling
holiday to Australia's Gold
Coast. This was the first time
my wife and I have ever been
there.We were not very impressed
- the traffic was like the M25
and Surfers was like little
Tokyo.All Japanese shops selling
tourist junk to the Japanese.
There are some lovely beaches
with plenty of room on them,
but the rest of it is like
Blackpool or Brighton - seedy
and in need of a good clean up.

We had a day further up on the
Sunshine coast. This was much
better, not so crowded and
better countryside. But in
spite of it all we enjoyed
ourselves and would go there
again.

If there is any news about the
newer version of PROCROSS could
you olease let me know. I would
like to have a few more charact-
ers for clues.

All the best from...

                Alan Rutherford

Brian Cavers to Alan Rutherford

I have had little time to do any
more to PROCROSS which is a real
shame because I must have done
nine tenths of the improvements.
As I remember I was at the test-
ing stage but there was one bad
machine code bug that was inter-
mittent so extremely difficult
to track down. The only other
thing I think that needs to be
done is to create a cutdown ver-
sion for use in OUTLET.

So many projects are on a shelf
waiting my attention but I have
now moved PROCROSS into my IN
tray so at least it should get
looked at over the next few
months!                 Brian

The other main problem is that we have huge stocks of disk and address labels which are on tractor feed backing and are not suitable to use with an InkJet.

We managed to get by last month using an old "banger" dot matrix held together with sticks and chewing gum but it caused some headaches and and the whole episode contributed towards the delay in getting out last months OUTLET magazine.

On the plus side is the great graphics capability (which we have not yet fully explored), the marvellous print quality, and I can now print my letters at five in the morning (I'm a bit of an insomniac) without waking the rest of the house.

Если вы загрузите, скажем, OUTLET 120 (текущий), затем вставите диск с OUTLET 76 и выберете B для писем, он должен загрузить старые письма, и вы сможете их распечатать.

Если имя файла отличается, вам сначала нужно найти старое имя, сделав CAT старого выпуска, и определить нужный файл (текстовые файлы OUTLET всегда заканчиваются на .#). Затем...

1. Войдите в +3 BASIC.
2. Введите MERGE "CONTENTS"
3. Введите LIST 30
4. Замените первый пункт с "EDIT'L  .#" на старое имя файла, которое вы увидели в CAT, и нажмите ENTER, чтобы обновить строку.
5. Введите RUN
6. Вставьте старый выпуск в привод A.
7. Выберите EDITORIAL, старый файл должен загрузиться, и вы сможете его распечатать.

Заметьте, что старый файл вовсе не обязательно должен быть редакционной статьей, это может быть DRIVECHAT, INFO или что угодно, просто удобнее подставить его первым пунктом.

Этот метод должен работать на любой системе, за исключением того, что в ранних выпусках OUTLET не использовалось расширение .#, поэтому там также потребуется изменить строку 200.
